summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose ~95% YoY to ~INR 159 crore, EBITDA ~INR 46.7 crore at 29.3% margin, unexecuted order book INR 846 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 revenue of ~INR 159 crore (up ~95% YoY), EBITDA of INR 46.7 crore (up ~110%) and PAT of INR 31.2 crore (up ~95%), with a 29.3% EBITDA margin. Debtor days fell from 210 to 178 and inventory days from 313 to 259 over six months. Management said the unexecuted order book stood at INR 846 crore as of 30 September 2026, against an opening INR 697 crore, and targeted a 40-50% revenue CAGR over three to five years. Key uncertainties remained on Kavach approved-vendor status, which is still in trials with no timeline given, and on the main board migration, which is awaiting eligibility.

financial_highlights.change: down from 210 days in six months
opening FY27 INR 697 crore; H1 inflow INR 308 crore

segments.name: Locomotive subsystems (ex-Advanced Rail, now merged)
segments.commentary: Management said more than 80% of current revenue and about 80% of the future order book (excluding Kavach) come from locomotive subsystems and green mobility. Advanced Rail is now a single unit with Concord.

segments.name: Kavach / railway safety (via Progota associate, 46.5% stake)
segments.commentary: Progota is an associate, so only profit share is booked, not revenue consolidation. Management said Kavach is still in trials for approved-vendor status; no timeline given. Shareholder query on Kavach segment revenue was deferred to the IR team.

segments.name: Fusion (PCB / EMS, acquired)
segments.commentary: Backward integration into PCB, PCB assembly and SMT EMS has started. Management expects around INR 400 crore revenue at full scale; plant described as production ready, and first revenue hoped for in FY27.

segments.name: Green mobility / propulsion
segments.commentary: One battery locomotive delivered and running for over 12 months. A green hydrogen propulsion order is to be executed next year, and a 3100 HP hydrogen loco is in development. IGBT propulsion is in development.

guidance_outlook: Targeting a revenue CAGR of about 40-50% over the next three to five years, which management said implies roughly INR 1,000 crore revenue by FY30 when a shareholder raised it, without confirming that number.
H2 has historically been about 60% of the year's revenue versus 40% in H1; management expects the same pattern in FY27 and ex-Kavach growth of similar magnitude next year.
International markets expected to contribute one-fourth to one-half of revenue over three to five years; a few orders of a few million dollars possible in the current or next year.
Fusion expected to marginally improve profitability by some basis points in FY28.
Management said margins of 29-30% are sustainable, citing in-house technology.
capex_capacity: Fusion installed capacity exceeds 2 lakh sq m of flex PCB, plus additional rigid PCB capacity.
Management expects to use 30-40% of Fusion's SMT/PCBA capability for internal needs, with rigid PCB use only marginal.
Fusion plant described as production ready; Fusion exhibiting at Electronica Germany after Diwali.
Hydrogen propulsion system to be deployed by early next year per management.
No fundraise planned in the near term based on the current order book; working capital said to be adequately covered by banks.
demand_pricing: Kavach: management said roughly 10% of the Kavach opportunity is deployed so far and the programme runs over 10-15 years; new competition expected but seen as having long gestation.
Non-Kavach order book addition of INR 100-plus crore from locomotive subsystems and real-time monitoring and sensing applications.
Kavach orders carry a 12-month delivery period per management, though the company is not yet an approved vendor.
Price variation clauses in railway tenders differ; where unavailable, component cost rises from geopolitical issues are absorbed. Fusion work for third parties is a complete pass-through.
Discussions with 3 or 4 companies (e.g. HBL, Kernex named by analyst) to sell flex/rigid PCB and PCBA.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for Progota developer-to-approved-vendor status for Kavach.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said trials are progressing and the outcome will come soon, but declined to give any date or number.

qa_highlights.question: Status of main board migration.
qa_highlights.answer: Eligibility to be completed very soon; applications to be filed immediately after.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue would a Kavach order add to Concord, given Progota is an associate?
qa_highlights.answer: Progota is 46.5% owned and is equity-accounted, so only profit share appears; no line-by-line revenue consolidation. Management said revenue is growing without Kavach.

qa_highlights.question: Share of H1 and backlog from Advanced Rail/locomotive versus legacy business.
qa_highlights.answer: Over 80% of current revenue and about 80% of future order book, ex-Kavach, is locomotive subsystems and green mobility.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins of 29-30% be the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are a focus and expects to sustain them with economies of scale and in-house technology; no numerical guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Best-guess FY27 and FY28 revenue.
qa_highlights.answer: No number given. Management reiterated H2 is typically about 60% of annual revenue and 40-50% CAGR target.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and fundraise plans before main board migration.
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital adequately covered by banks; no fundraise planned on the current order book, citing OpEx reasons.

risks_watch: Kavach approved-vendor status is still pending and has no timeline; Kavach orders carry 12-month delivery periods.
Kavach revenue is booked through the 46.5% associate Progota, so consolidated revenue does not capture Kavach order value.
Receivables of 178 days remain high; a shareholder asked about the INR 141 crore receivable balance and management did not answer directly.
Fusion plant ramp-up and PCB component price increases from geopolitical factors may not fully pass through in railway tenders.
The 40-50% CAGR target, and the implied ~INR 1,000 crore FY30 revenue, rest on pipeline conversion that management did not quantify by platform.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, margins and the 40-50% CAGR target, but evasive on Kavach approval timelines, Kavach revenue split, and platform-level sizing. Management repeatedly deferred specifics to later updates.
key_quotes: The revenue has grown up by almost ~95% year on year to ~INR 159 crores.
So, debtor days have reduced from 210 to 178 days in just these 6 months.
We are hopeful for that. The trials are going on.
Based on the current order book, I don't see a fundraise opportunity coming in for primarily OpEx reasons.

growth.why: Management targets a 40-50% revenue CAGR over 3-5 years (midpoint 40-45%, recorded as 40), backed by an unexecuted order book of INR 846 crore at 30 Sep 2026 (up from INR 697 crore) and production-ready Fusion PCB/EMS capacity expected to reach ~INR 400 crore revenue at full scale, though no quarterly-specific growth figure or Kavach approval timeline was given.

rows.why: Unexecuted order book rose to INR 846 crore at 30 Sep 2026 from INR 697 crore (H1 inflow INR 308 crore), and H1 revenue grew ~95% YoY, with H2 typically ~60% of annual revenue.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Kavach approved-vendor status has no timeline, Kavach orders carry 12-month delivery periods, and receivable days remain high at 178 against a 40-50% CAGR target that rests on unquantified pipeline conversion.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Hydrogen propulsion system is to be deployed by early next year (under construction, Q2 FY28 per the brief), with a green hydrogen propulsion order to be executed next year and a 3100 HP hydrogen loco in development.

rows.label: Kavach approved-vendor status via Progota

rows.label: Main board migration

rows.label: International orders

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, the 40-50% CAGR target, Fusion capacity and 29-30% margins, but evasive on Kavach approval timing, Kavach revenue split and the INR 141 crore receivable balance, while analysts pushed on those points and on platform-level sizing.
